_comment: TEMPLATE, WITH ONE EXCEPTION (see _authorship_exception_comment). Real per-machine config -- paths, secrets, roots, transports -- lives in config/local.json (gitignored) and OVERRIDES these entries. This file documents the shape and provides a safe 'default' base layer. Keyed by socket.gethostname() -- run 'python run.py config' to see a machine's hostname. 'roots' = estate roots whose CHILD folders are the projects to scan (omit for legacy sibling discovery). Copy an example below into config/local.json, rename the key to your hostname, and fill in real paths.
_authorship_exception_comment: 'authors' is the one real machine fact this file carries, and local.json CANNOT override it -- l5gntools.config.authored_artefacts reads authorship from this file alone (config._tracked_entry). DECISIONS 0054 clause 6: authorship is estate policy and lives in the tracked file only. The two contracts collided on 2026-08-31: this file said 'no real machine data' while clause 6 said authorship must live in a tracked file, which between them made the clause unsatisfiable -- every real host existed only in local.json, so the 'authors' key here sat under a RENAME-ME placeholder no hostname ever matched and was never read. Nothing noticed, because no auditor or tester reads this file (every config tester is hermetic against a temp fixture). A host section here may therefore carry a real hostname and an 'authors' list AND NOTHING ELSE; its paths still belong in local.json. The reason authorship is exempt: an untracked declaration makes 'no host declares this artefact' and 'the declaration has not been shipped here yet' the same input with two meanings, and 0053 clause 5's pin-bump refusal is what rests on telling them apart.
_is_project_comment: A root may carry 'is_project': true, meaning THIS PATH IS THE PROJECT rather than a folder whose children are projects. Use it for a project that sits outside every container root -- naming its parent instead would drag in every unrelated sibling, and naming it as a normal root would turn its own subfolders into projects. It is also the only way L5GN-Tools scans itself: discover_projects() skips TOOLKIT_ROOT on every container walk, so the toolkit is scanned only where a producer has declared it explicitly (DECISIONS 0020; personal rig only).
_roots_comment: 'roots' accepts either a bare path string or {'path': ..., 'scope': 'l5gn'|'mcf'}. The tagged form is how a project gets its registry scope (DECISIONS 0012): scope is declared on the root in the PRODUCER's config, never inferred from folder nesting. That is deliberate -- the layout differs on every machine (the knight has an L5GN folder and no MCF, the gaming rig is flat, the work rig has both), so nesting has never been a reliable signal. Tagging the root gets the same answer with no folder reorg. An untagged root still scans fine; its projects land as scope 'other' and are listed in build_registry --report-aliases under DEPOSIT GAPS.
_default_comment: 'default' is a BASE LAYER UNDER A MATCHED HOST, never a fallback for an unmatched one. A hostname listed in neither this file nor local.json raises config.UnknownHostError; it does not quietly resolve to these values. That is deliberate -- a rootless 'default' answering for an unknown host is how a run somewhere it was never meant to run (a sandbox, a fresh box, a renamed machine) produces a confident snapshot of an empty estate. Run 'python run.py config' to see this machine's hostname; it is the one command that still reports on an unconfigured host.
_authors_comment: 'authors' lists the repo-relative artefacts THIS host authors. 'run.py pin bump' refuses any artefact not listed for the host it runs on (DECISIONS 0053 clause 5): bumping a pin from a hand-copied stale artefact commits a wrong fingerprint over the authoritative one and turns the gate green, which is worse than the red it clears. Authorship is per-ARTEFACT and cannot be carried by 'role' -- this estate has two 'producer' hosts and the question is which of them authors a given file. An artefact no host declares is refused everywhere: that is a config gap reported as one, never read as permission.
_real_hosts_comment: Real hostnames below carry 'authors' and nothing else. They are not templates and must not be renamed. A host that appears only in local.json authors nothing -- that is the correct answer and not a gap, because authorship it cannot ship is authorship no other checkout can see.

RENAME-ME-GAMING-RIG._authors_note: The 'authors' key that used to sit here was inert: this is a template key and no real hostname ever matched it, so nothing read it. The live declaration is under the real host section above. Shape shown in _authors_comment.

RENAME-ME-WORK-LAPTOP._authors_note: No 'authors' key: this host holds a hand-copied conversation map and authors none of it. That absence is what makes 'run.py pin bump' refuse here, which is the whole point.

_transcripts_comment: 'cli_transcripts_home' / 'cowork_transcripts_home' -- machine facts for chronicler/pipeline/local_transcripts.py (COWORK_BRIEF_local_transcript_intake.md Phase 1). Both are per-user, machine-specific paths (Claude Code's ~/.claude/projects, and the Cowork desktop app's MSIX-virtualised LocalCache session root -- NOT %APPDATA%\Claude, which is a virtualised view a normal process can't see). Absent key -> that store is reported as 'not configured', not an error. The packaged-app id in the Cowork path is per-install; find it by browsing to %LOCALAPPDATA%/Packages and looking for the Claude_* folder.
_census_comment: 'run.py census' is role-aware. A producer censuses its 'roots'. A consumer censuses two roots: the deployed toolkit ('code_root', optional -- it defaults to the toolkit the command is running from, which IS the deploy) and the vault ('chronicler_home'). Both resolved here, never hardcoded.
